name: AX30G Reverb -- four parallel feedback combs (tapped twice, once per output) into a per-channel Schroeder allpass cascade; measured 2026-09-18
notes: Derivation: docs/rev-model-2026-09-18.md, from the hot-broadband REV capture set (-6 dBFS click / 5 s sweep / 60 ms burst at Balance 50). It supersedes the candidate-A model of docs/rev-identification-2026-09-17.md, which was known wrong.

Structure per Type: predelay -> a per-channel pure input delay -> FOUR parallel feedback combs (each a plain recirculating delay, no filter unless High Damp is up) -> each comb is read at ONE position per output channel, the four reads summed with equal weight -> a three-section series Schroeder allpass cascade, its own lengths per channel -> wet, inverted.

Every allpass is y[n] = u*v[n] + v[n-L] - u*y[n-L] (a Schroeder allpass with a NEGATIVE coefficient), the sign pattern the unit shows (+,+,-,+ along each element's own echo series). Sections whose LENGTH is shared between L and R also share u, to the measurement's 0.3 %.
comb read offsets are given in each channel's own frame, i.e. after input_delay[channel]; several exceed the comb's own length (PLATE), which a delay line longer than its feedback tap supplies.

Rev Time law: comb gain g_i = 10^(-3*rt_length_i/(RevTime*fs)) -- each comb's own RT60 IS the displayed Rev Time in seconds. rt_length equals the comb's delay for ROOM and HALL; for PLATE's two short combs it is twice the delay (measured: those two decay at exactly 2x the rate per sample that a common RT60 would give).

High Damp: one first-order lowpass in each comb's feedback path, pole a. The coefficients are fitted by simulation against the per-octave decay of the click tails and are the weakest part of this model (see the report's uncertainties).
Balance is a crossfade; the wet and dry tables are measured, eight points each.
